title: On Energy References when a Magnetic Field is Applied. A Practical Guide to Reference Energies with and without a Magnetic Field
abstract: We present a simple analysis of the energy references and of the magnetic-field-dependent and system-dependent features of the Landau energy levels. The energy reference used in describing Landau quantization is usually taken as given, with the Fermi levels of the electron system and the coupled reservoir aligned in thermal equilibrium. Nevertheless, the dependence of the Landau-level spectrum on magnetic field can make the relation between these energy references less transparent. In this work, we show that when a magnetic field is applied and the confined Landau levels $E_n$ are established, both the Fermi level $E_F$ and the bottom energy $E_0$ remain fixed when the magnetic field varies. We show that the bottom energy $E_0$ is independent of $B$, and determined by a system-dependent field $B_1$, defined by the condition that the first Landau level equals the Fermi energy. In contrast, the minimum of the parabolic well depends explicitly on the magnetic field. The resulting picture provides a simple way of displaying the relative motion of the Landau levels and the fixed Fermi level without introducing a magnetic-field-dependent energy zero.
summary: This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis to resolve the ambiguity of energy references when studying Landau quantization in a magnetic field. It demonstrates that while the confining potential minimum varies with the magnetic field, the Fermi level and the bottom energy of the Landau spectrum remain fixed references. This clarification offers a simpler, more consistent picture for interpreting quantum Hall measurements.
main_problem: The paper addresses the ambiguity in defining the appropriate energy reference point when analyzing Landau quantization in a 2D electron system subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field.
main_result: It shows that while the Landau level spacing and the parabolic well minimum depend explicitly on the magnetic field, the Fermi level ($E_F$) and the bottom energy ($E_0$) can be shown to remain fixed references for a given system.
method: The analysis involves comparing the magnetic field dependence of various energy levels ($E_n$, $E_0$, $E_{\min}$) using theoretical derivations based on the physical constraints of the system.
model_or_system: The model is a charged particle confined in a two-dimensional system (like graphene) subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field, leading to the formation of discrete Landau energy levels.
key_observables: Landau energy levels ($E_n$), bottom energy ($E_0$), confining potential minimum ($E_{\min}$), and the Fermi level ($E_F$).
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength ($B$), cyclotron frequency ($\omega_c$), and the system-dependent field $B_1$ defined by $E_1(B_1) = E_F$.
main_assumptions: The standard Landau quantization framework is assumed, and the Fermi level is fixed by an external reservoir in thermal equilibrium.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the energy reference alignment in two parts: (a) the general setup, and (b) the local representation showing the relationship between $E_0$, $E_{\min}$, and the Landau levels.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the dependence of the key energy components ($E_n$, $E_0$, $E_{\min}$) on the magnetic field $B$, ultimately establishing which references remain constant and which vary.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for interpreting experimental measurements in quantum Hall systems, clarifying how to correctly set the energy zero point when analyzing field-dependent spectra.
